### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**48** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 78 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b0a62a912c32f9e97e676d040a907842b4db55aa` — the merge of head `5eb62f096eec61828542a2bba3bfa57628843f61` into base `57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b0a62a912c32f9e97e676d040a907842b4db55aa && git checkout b0a62a912c32f9e97e676d040a907842b4db55aa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc 5eb62f096eec61828542a2bba3bfa57628843f61 && git checkout -B drift-repro 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc && git merge --no-ff 5eb62f096eec61828542a2bba3bfa57628843f61

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `472e55cbb64665dfac1dab6a0b8e2bcfa7a2b9d2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/credential-evaluation-guard.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/credential-evaluation-guard.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-number-comparand-declared-type-door.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-text-operator-declared-type-door.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/encrypted-field-behavior.dogfood.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/secret-fields.ts (`collectCredentialFields`, `collectMaskedReadFields`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`lowerWhereFilterArray`, `fillQueryAstDefaults`, `lowerRelationConditions`, `expandRelatedRecords`, `expandSearchOnAst`, `mergeReadContext`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`findData`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts (`assertNoInternalFieldEvaluated`, `refuseInternalInFilter`, `refuseInternalInExpand`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-guard.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts (`findExisting`), packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts (`referenceTargetOf`), packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts (`FilterConditionSchema`, `FieldReferenceSchema`), packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts and packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts (array-form refusal at the driver), docs/adr/0100-credential-field-channels.md, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, packages/objectql/CHANGELOG.md (the #22646 entry).

Face: narrowing. The diff touches no `packages/spec/src/**` non-test path and no governed path; the PR body itself states "This PR narrows a query shape that was accepted before" and asks for a contract-review-tier review, and the maintainer dispatched one. The scope floor on this face is every path of the diff outside the prose faces; the changeset and the two `content/docs` pages are the lane seat's at ACCEPT, read here only for the declaration in ②.

Security-hardening ruling: this record names positions and refusals; it carries no reproduction.

### ① Derived judgments

The accept set the diff changes, read off the code:

1. **`where` on a `password` / `secret` column, every verb, non-system caller.** Previously evaluated; now `400 INVALID_FIELD` before the driver. Correct. Order verified in `engine.ts`: `find` folds aliases, refuses unknown options, runs `lowerWhereFilterArray` (array form to object form, the declared-type doors), fills AST defaults, then calls `rejectCredentialEvaluation`, then expands `search`, then the middleware chain. `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate`, `update`, `delete` call it at the same relative position (after `lowerWhereFilterArray`, before any token resolution, search expansion, middleware or driver). Every logical branch (`$and` / `$or` / `$not`) and a dotted key's head segment are walked. Matches the claim.
2. **A `{ $field }` comparand naming a credential column.** Collected from any comparand position, head segment of the reference. `FieldReferenceSchema` is a plain string and both the predicate guard and this walker read its first segment, so a cross-object spelling has no reader anywhere; no gap there. Correct.
3. **`orderBy` on a credential column.** For `find` / `findOne` the AST's `orderBy` is already `SortNodeSchema`-parsed (`{ field, order }`) when the guard runs; the guard also reads the string spelling and a leading `-`. The wire-only `sort` alias is folded by the protocol and refused at a direct engine call. Correct.
4. **`aggregations[i].filter`.** Walked per aggregation, located at `aggregations[i].filter`. The aggregate half (`rejectCredentialAggregation`: group-by and operand) is unchanged and still runs after it. Correct.
5. **`expand` entries' own `where` / `orderBy`, every depth, judged against `referenceTargetOf(def)`.** Correct, and necessary: `expandRelatedRecords` re-enters `this.find` on the target with the caller's context, which would refuse too, but that path catches the sub-read's refusal and retains the bare id, so without the pre-judgment the refusal would be swallowed into a silent drop. A targetless or non-reference field is skipped by both the guard and `expandRelatedRecords` on the same predicate, so no read happens there. Correct.
6. **Nested-relation condition (`{ lookup: { credential: … } }`).** Deliberately not walked by the guard; `lowerRelationConditions` reads the related object through `this.find` with the caller's execution context, which passes through the guard against the related object's own fields; a refusal propagates ("nothing is swallowed"). The unit test pins it. Correct.
7. **Array-form (`[field, op, value]`) spellings in nested positions** (an `expand` entry's `where`, a per-aggregation `filter`, a `$and` / `$or` member). The guard reads the object form only, and `lowerWhereFilterArray` lowers only the top-level `where`. Judged not a gap: nothing below the top level lowers a tuple (the engine and the protocol call `parseFilterAST` on the top-level `where` only; `FilterConditionSchema` types `$and` / `$or` members as records; the memory driver refuses an array that reaches it and reads a `$and` child's keys, which for a tuple are `0`, `1`, `2`; the SQL driver refuses at its door), so no component evaluates a credential column through that spelling. The walker's shape matches what can execute.
8. **Search scan set.** Credential columns are now withheld from the set the search expansion resolves over, including an author-declared `searchableFields` entry, for every verb that reaches `expandSearchOnAst` (`find` / `findOne` / `aggregate` / `count` through `expandSearchOnOptions`). The guard runs before the expansion, so the expansion's server-authored `$or` is never judged as the caller's predicate. Correct. See ③-c for what this leaves silently inert.
9. **System-context exemption.** The guard returns only on `context.isSystem === true`. The wire cannot supply it: protocol `findData` deletes any inbound `context` unconditionally before setting the server-derived one, and `enforceAuth` documents that `isSystem` is never set on inbound HTTP; `update` / `delete` read `options.context`, which the protocol's write doors set from the dispatcher's context. `mergeReadContext` merges two server-built contexts. Correct. The system-context register row 18c and the regenerated per-symbol table name the one read.
10. **Presence checks (`null`, `$null`, `$exists`, `$empty` with a boolean operand, `$eq: null`, `$ne: null`, `$not` over any of those).** Keeping them is safe, on three readings. (a) Set-or-unset is what every masked read already serves (`SECRET_MASK` for a set value, `null` for an unset one, ADR-0100 A and B), so the check reveals nothing beyond the row. (b) A caller withheld the column by field-level security never reaches the row's answer either: plugin-security's `assertReadableQueryFields` collects a condition's key regardless of operator and refuses `403` on the caller's own AST (it runs after this guard, before RLS injection), unchanged by this PR; so the presence check serves exactly the callers the row already serves. (c) The empty string is unwritable into either type since #8559 (`EmptyCredentialWriteError`), so `$empty` cannot distinguish a third state. The operand typing is strict (a non-boolean `$null`, an empty object, a mixed operator set are refused). The default is the safe one, and the product question the dev raised is answered: keep.
11. **`collectCredentialFields` is exemption-free**, so a `password`-typed column on a `managedBy: 'better-auth'` object is also refused to a non-system caller although its read is unmasked. Consistent with the aggregate half; ADR-0100 B4 pins that no shipped identity object declares one, and the auth subsystem's own lookups run as system. Accepted as designed.
12. **`internal: true` columns** stay at the generic data door (`assertNoInternalFieldEvaluated`); the dogfood case pins that door beside the password case. Unchanged, correct.
13. **A consequence the PR body does not name.** The import runner's upsert match (`findExisting` in `core/src/utils/import-runner.ts`) looks rows up through `findData` with the import's caller context, which the import doors never elevate; an upsert import whose `matchFields` names a credential column is therefore now refused inside that lookup. Fail-closed and correct; it belongs in the changeset's FROM / TO (should-fix 2).
14. **Doors.** REST `POST /data/:object/query` and `GET /data/:object?filter=…` are pinned on the booted showcase; flows, hooks' `ctx.api`, the MCP bridges and plugin routes reach the same six engine verbs with a caller context. The Console claim holds: `isMaskedColumnKey` in `data-table.tsx` already withholds sort and search on masked columns.
15. **Public surface.** One new module `credential-evaluation-guard.ts`; `rejectCredentialEvaluation` and `isCredentialPresenceCondition` are module exports but not re-exported from the package entry (no `index.ts` change in the diff). No published type changes. Census pins updated: the reference-target arbiter census (`second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts`, classified `not-a-served-read`, the REWORK round-1 fix) and the federated readers ledger (`caller-predicate`). Both classifications hold against the code: the guard reads declared fields from the registry and no record.

### ② Semver level

Declared: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `@objectstack/objectql: patch`. **The arm is wrong.** A query shape every non-system caller could write and have evaluated on `main` (a filter or sort key on a credential column) is now refused `400` at six verbs: that is an accept-set narrowing of a served runtime surface, the exact class `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` describes at its own prompt ("add `(narrowing)` if it narrows one, a BREAKING change, whatever its level") and the class the PR body itself names in its third sentence. The precedent is the `internal: true` evaluate door (#22646, `packages/objectql/CHANGELOG.md`): same positions (filter, sort, per-aggregation filter, nested-relation condition, expand tree, search set), same envelope, shipped as `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with a `**BREAKING** (an accept-set narrowing)` banner and one ADR-0087 marker in the `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` category. A `no` without the arm is the auditable false declaration landing-operations names, and it switches off both gates that read the arm (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` signal 4, the no-major gate's grade).

What is right and stays: `Metadata-protocol: none` (no key, value or metadata type an author writes changes; `searchableFields` keeps its shape) and the `patch` level (ruling A: a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING carriers). The Skills-docs line is owed by the arm: `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` teaches `type: 'secret'` and says nothing about querying it, and no eval exercises the refusal, so `updated here` is not claimable from this diff; `follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` (one sentence: a credential column is never a filter or sort key; only a has-a-value check) or `none — REASON` is the dev's declaration, read at ACCEPT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- (a) **Presence checks retained, raised as a product question.** Answered in ① item 10: safe, keep. No escalation.
- (b) **`internal: true` left at the data door "because some server-side consumers do not run as system".** Accepted: the two collectors stay independent on purpose, and the dogfood case pins both doors side by side.
- (c) **An author-declared `searchableFields` naming a credential column is now silently withheld**, where the #22646 precedent refuses an explicit `$searchFields` naming an `internal` column loudly at the door and ADR-0078 refuses silently inert metadata. Fail-closed on the leak axis, so not a defect of this PR; a spec-side refusal of such an entry (and the door's explicit-`searchFields` refusal extended to credential types) is a follow-up card (should-fix 1), not a rider here, since it changes what an author can write.
- (d) **Declared-type door tests driven as system for credential cells.** The fixture is right (the PASS rows reach the guard and need a system caller), but the comment's ordering claim ("refuses … before this door is reached") is inverted: `assertTextOperatorTargetsAreStringCapable` and `narrowNumberComparands` run inside `lowerWhereFilterArray`, before the guard. Same `400` class either way; wording only (should-fix 3).
- (e) `open_questions`: none in the PR body beyond (a). Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

On the narrowing face, against the published spec on `main`: the change takes no declared capability away at the consumer and makes the spec's own refusal real. ADR-0100 declares both channels masked on every generic read and names evaluation as the open leak class (its non-goals already called the aggregate position a refusal, shipped as #3171); a position that answers by the stored value contradicts that read-mask promise, and the `internal: true` door (#22646) settled that such positions are refused, not rewritten. The guard reads the one type-keyed collector the aggregate half reads, so the two halves cannot drift; it sits in the engine (not only at the data door) so every door with a caller context meets it; it answers in the ADR-0112 envelope with `param` locating the position; and it runs on the caller's own AST, before server-authored filters are injected, which is the ordering contract the predicate guard already states. The accepted shape is the minimal one that keeps the Console's and pickers' "is it set" use working without creating a second rule. Accepted against the scenario (checklist `records-forms.encrypted-field-behavior`, acceptance[4]) and the code it cites. Ablation evidence in the PR body (source- and dist-resolved, restore proven) is consistent with the test file read here; the record did not re-run it.

**Must-fix**

1. Declaration: in the changeset body and the PR body, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; keep `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch`; add the `**BREAKING** (an accept-set narrowing)` banner with a FROM / TO paragraph (the #22646 entry is the template); exactly one ADR-0087 HTML-comment marker in the changeset body, category `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, stating that no metadata key, spelling, export or stored shape moves and that what narrows is a runtime read door; and a `Skills-docs:` line in the PR body (② names the admissible values). Then re-run `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` locally.

**Should-fix**

1. File a follow-up card: refuse a `secret` / `password` entry in `searchableFields` at the spec door, and extend the data door's explicit-`searchFields` refusal to credential types, so the declaration is not silently inert (③-c).
2. Changeset FROM / TO: name the import upsert `matchFields` consequence (① item 13).
3. The two declared-type door test comments: state that the doors run first inside `lowerWhereFilterArray` and the guard answers the rows those doors pass (③-d).

Implemented-by: `claude/harden-credential-field-predicates`
Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcVy4VXmkQjn2MGeaWk`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

The refusal is complete across every position the PR claims, the system-context exemption is unreachable from the wire, and the presence check is safe to keep; the FAIL is the declaration alone (must-fix 1). A head that carries the corrected declaration and nothing else owes a delta review by this reviewer, not a full round.
